question: Should Windows script providers fail closed whenever Job Object containment cannot initialize, or should existing direct-shell fallback remain the default with strict containment made explicit?
rationale: The PR trades stronger descendant-process containment for a deliberate availability and upgrade-compatibility break, and repository evidence alone cannot determine which policy maintainers intend.

options.title: Keep compatibility by default
options.body: Retain direct-shell fallback for existing users and add an explicit strict-containment setting with tests for both modes.

options.title: Require containment unconditionally
options.body: Accept that affected Windows script providers will stop working and require upgrade documentation plus native failure-and-recovery proof.

options.title: Split the policy change
options.body: Land the recorder and lock-root fixes separately while holding the script fallback removal for a dedicated security-boundary decision.

recommendation.title: Keep compatibility by default
recommendation.body: Retain direct-shell fallback for existing users and add an explicit strict-containment setting with tests for both modes.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the complete hardening series and are the most directly connected repository member in the available evidence.
